Date: 2026-03-22
Time: 10:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Elena (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood Partner Ops), Carlos (Veridian Head Partnerships), Priya (Biz Dev), Aisha (Solutions Architect), Liam (Cloud Infra)
summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and Veridian Cloud. High-level discussion of joint GTM, integration points (marketplace listing, API connectors, bare-metal GPU co-located offering), technical constraints (networking/VPC peering, KMS, audit logs), and initial perf/compatibility checks. Agreed next steps to exchange integration spec, perf spreadsheet, and schedule infra deep-dive.
topics: Introductions; Go-to-market alignment; Technical integration surface (private connectors, VPC, dedicated pools); Security/compliance (SOC2, KMS, audit logs); Performance benchmarking (A100, H100 equivalents, quantized models); Commercial model and revenue share; Next steps and owners.
transcript:
00:00 Samir (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we really appreciate you taking the time. Quick round of intros?
00:12 Carlos (Veridian): Yeah hi all, Carlos here, I run partnerships at Veridian. Priya and Aisha are with me.
00:18 Priya (Veridian): Hi! excited to learn more about Redwood and see where we can collaborate.
00:22 Elena (Redwood SE): Hi folks, Elena, I'm the solutions engineer, I'll mostly do the tech questions.
00:27 Aisha (Veridian): Aisha, solutions architect, I'll be focused on networking and infra.
00:35 Samir (Redwood): Quick agenda, intro, what each of us sells, technical integration points, perf and next steps. Sound good?
02:05 Carlos: Yeah, to start, Veridian provides a cloud offering optimized for AI workloads, we do AKS-like managed k8s plus bare-metal GPU racks in US-east and EU-west. We also run a marketplace for ISVs.
02:30 Samir: Great, that's helpful. Our thesis at Redwood is serving-first inference, we do hosted API, dedicated reserved pools and private deployments. For partners we're looking to do marketplace listings and co-managed Dedicated pools where customers can route to Veridian capacity via our smart routing.
03:02 Priya: Curious on the technical surface — how would we route? Is it like a VPC peering or do you need an agent inside our network?
03:18 Elena: Good question. We have two patterns: private control plane with VPC peering where requests go over peered network to customer-managed infra, or a hybrid where we run a small control-plane agent and route inference traffic to your GPU fleet. The latter is common for partners where we don't want to expose full peering.
03:45 Liam (Veridian): So the agent needs outbound to Redwood control plane only? Any special ports?
03:52 Elena: Mostly outbound HTTPS, and a persistent gRPC tunnel for metrics and KV cache coordination. We also support mutual TLS + customer KMS for key wrapping.
04:20 Aisha: About data retention and logs — customers will need audit logs retained for 12 months, SOC2 is a must. How does Redwood handle audit logs if we run dedicated pools?
04:36 Samir: If it's Dedicated on Veridian, logs can be forwarded to your SIEM; we can ship agent logs or deliver log files via S3. For hosted, we retain per-customer audit trails and can export on demand. We have SOC2 compliance and can share certs.
05:05 Priya: Perfect. On the GTM side, we want to understand revenue share and marketplace listing requirements. Is there a standard?
05:18 Maya (Redwood Partner Ops): We typically do a 70/30 split for net new customers on marketplace sales, but flexible for strategic partners; also co-marketing funds for early pilots. We'll follow up with a partner program doc.
06:02 Carlos: Nice. On the technical side, we care about model compatibility — do you support quantized models (4-bit), and can you do kernel selection for different vendors (NVIDIA/Ampere/Hopper/AMD)?
06:18 Elena: Yes, our runtime supports quantized execution paths and can select kernels based on hardware; H100 and A100 are standard, we also have support for some non-NVIDIA backends though it's more experimental.
06:40 Aisha: Any constraints on model sizes or sequence lengths that lead to different placement? Like long-context models need special handling?
06:50 Elena: Correct, long context models can require KV sharding and higher memory. Our smart routing can pin such requests to instances with larger VRAM or split across multiple GPUs. We'll need to see workload samples.
07:25 Carlos: Can we run benchmarks jointly? we'd like to show our customers latency improvements when using Veridian infra.
07:32 Samir: Absolutely. Elena will share a perf spreadsheet template. We'd want a representative prompt set and seq lengths. Also, if you want, we can run a small canary using a dedicated pool for a pilot.
08:05 Priya: On security, do you integrate with external KMS like HashiCorp Vault or cloud KMS? We have a customer ask for HSM-backed keys.
08:15 Elena: We support customer-managed KMS via GCP KMS/Azure Key Vault/AWS KMS and also integrations to external HSMs for Private deployments; we can work through key wrapping.
09:00 Liam: Network egress costs — if routing inference to your control plane, we need to estimate cross-cloud egress, if kept in-region that's ok.
09:12 Samir: Agreed, routing policies can be region-aware; for Dedicated pools on Veridian we avoid cross-cloud egress entirely. We'll surface cost tradeoffs in the integration spec.
10:00 Carlos: On legal/compliance — we usually need a basic MSA + data processing addendum and a SOC2 attestation. How long does Redwood's procurement cycle normally take?
10:12 Samir: For partners it's usually 4-8 weeks depending on redlines. We'll introduce legal teams after we have scope.
11:05 Priya: Any red flags for customers moving to private deployments? Some of our customers have air-gapped requirements.
11:20 Elena: For air-gapped we can deliver an on-prem package; it's heavier but supported. The main work is image signing, offline license, and local KMS/HSM. We have done this two times in the past year.
12:00 Carlos: Great. Could you speak a bit more about the Dedicated product — autoscaling and burst capacity?
12:12 Samir: Dedicated provides reserved GPU pools with configurable autoscaling and optional burst to Redwood hosted capacity if you want overflow. You can set SLOs and autoscale triggers based on queue length or latency percentiles.
13:00 Aisha: For monitoring, do you expose traces and per-token cost breakdowns? Customers want to see token-level cost to map to billing.
13:12 Elena: Yes, Redwood Console exposes token-level cost, latency breakdowns, traces, and per-route dashboards. We also provide a tracing hook to your observability stack.
14:05 Priya: Excellent. On partner engineering effort — how much integration work for a marketplace connector?
14:20 Maya: Typical integration is 3-6 sprints depending on depth: basic listing + API integration could be 2-3 sprints, deeper co-managed dedicated offering with peering and SSO maybe 4-6 sprints.
15:10 Carlos: We should also discuss support model — will Redwood be involved in tier 2/3 support for customers on Veridian infra?
15:22 Samir: We usually operate a joint support model for partners with a runbook; Redwood can handle platform-level issues, Veridian handles infra and hardware. We'll create an escalation matrix.
16:00 Aisha: One technical ask: we need to know how KV cache warming works across restarts; do you persist cache to disk or rebuild on cold start?
16:12 Elena: We persist some cache and support prefix caching; cold starts rehydrate from persistent store but there's a warm-up period. We'll include details in the integration doc.
17:00 Liam: Regarding GPU SKUs, we have A100 and a limited H100 fleet; for benchmarking do you recommend specific batch sizes and quant profiles?
17:12 Elena: We'll recommend batch sizes based on model and latency targets; for 4-bit quant we typically see 2-3x throughput improvements but need to validate quality. We'll provide suggested quant profiles.
18:00 Carlos: Anything else on commercialization? we want to align on co-marketing and a pilot customer list.
18:18 Maya: We'll propose a pilot framework: 1 technical pilot with perf targets, 1 joint case study if metrics are met, 2 co-marketing plays.
19:05 Priya: ok awesome. Next steps recap?
19:12 Samir: Recap: Samir sends partner deck + integration spec; Elena shares perf template + initial perf numbers; Aisha sends sample workload and latency/SLOs; schedule tech deep-dive with Liam. Legal intro to follow.
19:40 Carlos: Works for us. We'll expect the doc early next week.
20:00 Elena: I'll also attach a short note on agent network ports and KMS flow.
20:12 Priya: Thanks everyone. Looking forward to the next call.
20:30 [meeting ends]
